source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 11: show-that using an odd integrand on [-1, 1]; book p. 102. No printed answer (show that).

blocks.explanation:
Yeh symmetric interval \([-1, 1]\) par saboot ka sawal hai, aur \(f\) koi bhi function ho sakta hai.
Diya kya hai? Left side mein extra factor \((1 - x)\) hai.
Kya saabit karna hai? Ke yeh extra \(-x\) wala hissa koi farq nahi dalta.
Rule kaunsa? \((1 - x)f(1 - x^2)\) ko do hisson mein torenge: \(f(1 - x^2)\) aur \(x f(1 - x^2)\). Doosra hissa odd hai, aur Property V ke mutabiq odd function ka symmetric interval par integral 0 hota hai.
Plan: torna, odd saabit karna, Property V.
steps:
Diya gaya: koi bhi continuous function \(f\).
Saabit karna: \(\int_{-1}^{1} (1 - x)f(1 - x^2)\,dx = \int_{-1}^{1} f(1 - x^2)\,dx\).
Tareeqa: Property IX se torna, phir Property V (\([-a, a]\) par odd function). Symmetric limits dekh kar odd/even ka khayal sab se pehle aana chahiye.

Integral ko torein
\[\int_{-1}^{1} (1 - x)f(1 - x^2)\,dx\]
\[= \int_{-1}^{1} f(1 - x^2)\,dx - \int_{-1}^{1} x f(1 - x^2)\,dx\]
Kyun: \((1 - x)\) ko multiply kar ke kholna, phir Property IX: farq ka integral integrals ka farq hai.

Doosra integrand odd hai
\[h(x) = x f(1 - x^2)\]
\[h(-x) = (-x)f\big(1 - (-x)^2\big)\]
\[= -x f(1 - x^2) = -h(x)\]
Kyun: \((-x)^2 = x^2\), is liye \(f(1 - x^2)\) bilkul nahi badla (yeh even hissa hai), lekin bahar wala \(x\) ban gaya \(-x\). Even times odd hamesha odd hota hai.
Dhyan dein: \(f\) ka formula na hone ke bawajood odd/even ka faisla ho sakta hai, kyunke \(f\) ke andar sirf \(x^2\) hai.

Property V lagayein
\[\int_{-1}^{1} x f(1 - x^2)\,dx = 0\]
\[\int_{-1}^{1} (1 - x)f(1 - x^2)\,dx = \int_{-1}^{1} f(1 - x^2)\,dx\]
Kyun: odd function ka \([-a, a]\) par integral 0; is liye sirf pehla hissa bacha, jo bilkul right side hai.

Tasdeeq: ek misaal se
\[f(u) = u:\ \int_{-1}^{1} (1 - x)(1 - x^2)\,dx = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
\[\int_{-1}^{1} (1 - x^2)\,dx = \dfrac{4}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(f(u) = u\) lene se extra hissa \(-\int_{-1}^{1} (x - x^3)\,dx\) banta hai, jo odd hone ki wajah se 0 hai; dono sides \(\frac{4}{3}\).
